w10_T4_003099: In the morning a bakery baked 200 cookies in each of 9 batches and divided them equally among its 5 shops. In the afternoon the first shop received 9 more cookies from a neighbour and sold 49 cookies. The delivery van is 4 metres long. In the evening the first shop gave half of the cookies it had left to a homeless shelter. How many cookies did the first shop have left?
w10_T4_003100: Ada had 53 marbles and won 36 more at recess. She then gave 88 marbles to Ben, so Ben now has many more marbles than Ada. At the swap table she traded each marble she had left for 2 shiny ones. Her aunt then gave her 9 more marbles. How many marbles does Ada have now?
w10_T4_003101: Mo's sweet shop had 146 chocolate bars and sold 95 of them. He snapped every remaining bar into 2 halves and packed the halves 3 to a bag. Each bag sells for 4 dollars, and Mo prices in dollars although a hundred cents make a dollar. He sold 21 bags, and 3 bags were damaged and thrown away. How many bags of chocolate halves does Mo have left?
w10_T4_003103: Kim put 25 dollars into her savings jar every week for 7 weeks, then added 74 dollars from her birthday. Her grandfather then doubled whatever was in the jar. A month later her grandmother matched the jar too, so it held twice as much as before her gift. Finally Kim added 30 dollars from babysitting. How many dollars are in Kim's jar now?
w10_T4_003107: A choir printed 209 song sheets and then 46 more. The sheets were divided equally among its 3 sections, and the altos took their share. The altos handed out 80 of their sheets at a concert that lasted ninety minutes, an hour and a half. The choir has 60 singers. After the concert 34 sheets were handed back to the altos' pile. How many sheets are in the altos' pile now?
w10_T4_003108: A factory has 184 machines, each running 3 shifts a day and turning out 9 parts per shift; each shift lasts four hundred and eighty minutes, that is, eight hours. On Monday the factory also received 40 parts from a subcontractor and 56 parts from a returned order, all added to the day's stock. The factory has 2 gates. Every part in that stock was sold for 8 dollars. How many dollars did Monday's stock sell for?
w10_T4_003116: In the morning a bike hire shop had 118 bikes in its rack. Before noon 71 bikes were hired out, and then 24 more. In the afternoon 10 bikes were returned, followed by 11 more. A day's hire costs 5 dollars. In the evening 69 bikes were returned. How many bikes were in the rack at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_003117: Ria had 174 beads, but 27 were chipped and thrown away. She divided the rest equally into 3 jars and kept one jar. At the craft fair she traded every bead in her jar for 8 tiny seed beads each. She gave 20 seed beads to her cousin Sana. Then she split all her remaining seed beads equally among herself, Sana and Mo, so that Sana ended up with more seed beads than Ria. How many seed beads does Ria have?
w10_T4_003118: Uma's flower farm has 89 rows, each row has 2 beds, each bed holds 5 plants, each plant has 4 stems, and each stem carries 9 blooms. The farm covers 12 hectares. This week Uma sold 22550 blooms to florists. Her rival Lev has fewer blooms left on his farm than Uma. How many blooms does Uma have left?
w10_T4_003119: In the morning Tom set out 150 bags of oranges with 5 oranges in every bag, tipped into one big crate, and by noon he had sold 523 oranges to a dozen customers. In the afternoon a juice bar bought every orange left in the crate at 9 cents each. In the evening the juice bar's owner sent over a 23-cent tip. Tom's neighbour Eve took in less at her stall than Tom did from the juice bar. How many cents did Tom receive from the juice bar altogether?
w10_T4_003120: Zed collected 116 shells a day on the beach, which is 3 kilometres long, for 5 days. He threw away 11 broken shells. At the shell market he traded every shell for 2 pearls, then every pearl for 9 coins, and each coin was worth 8 cents; he counts in cents although a hundred cents make a dollar. He then shared all the cents equally among himself and 3 friends, so 4 people got equal shares. His friend Ivy, who collected shells on her own, ended up with less than Zed. How many cents did Zed get?
w10_T4_003121: A beekeeper's storeroom held 137 jars of honey. She added 3 jars from the last of the spring batch and 32 jars from the summer batch. Then 2 jars broke on the shelf, and she added 25 jars from a late batch. The storeroom is 4 metres wide. She sold every jar in the storeroom at 6 dollars each. How many dollars did she take in?
w10_T4_003125: Leo went to the funfair with 177 dollars and spent 54 dollars on the entry ticket. He changed all his remaining dollars into ride tokens at 6 tokens per dollar, but after half an hour the rides shut for rain, so he changed all the tokens back into dollars at the same rate of 6 tokens per dollar. He spent 50 dollars on dinner and 57 dollars on a jacket. His friend Max went home with more money than Leo. How many dollars did Leo have when he went home?
w10_T4_003129: Mira bought 12 packs of socks with 2 socks in every pack and put them all in her drawer. Her mother added 59 socks from the wash, her aunt sent 6 socks, her grandmother sent 25 socks, and Mira found 8 more under the bed, all of which went into the drawer. Her brother Sol has fewer socks in his drawer than Mira. How many socks are in Mira's drawer now?
w10_T4_003136: At half past six in the morning, a garden water butt held 39 litres. A morning shower added 77 litres, and an afternoon storm added another 77 litres. The gardener poured in 13 litres from a bucket, and a final drizzle added 34 litres. How many litres are in the water butt now?
w10_T4_003143: Ana and Ben kept a joint savings jar that held 207 dollars. Their grandmother added 71 dollars, and then they spent 50 dollars from the jar on a board game. The jar is 30 centimetres tall. They split the remaining money into 2 equal shares, one each. Ana spent 94 dollars of her share on a bike helmet, so Ben now has more money left than Ana. How many dollars does Ana have left?
w10_T4_003149: In the morning a wholesaler unloaded 115 crates of apples; each crate held 7 boxes and each box held 7 apples, all tipped into one huge bin. A farmer added 72 loose apples to the bin. In the afternoon 4832 apples were sold to a supermarket, and 69 apples were returned to the bin from a cancelled order. In the evening 822 apples were sold to a cider maker. How many apples were left in the bin?
w10_T4_003155: In the morning a bakery baked 24 trays of pies with 3 pies on each tray, but 6 pies were burnt and thrown away. In the afternoon 40 whole pies were sold. The bakery has 5 staff. In the evening each remaining pie was cut into 9 slices for the cafe counter, and 21 slices of a different pie were added to the counter. How many slices were on the counter?
w10_T4_003158: Sami had 201 stamps and gave 92 of them to his friend Lia. At a stamp swap he doubled his collection, coming home with twice as many stamps as he had taken. His uncle then gave him 73 stamps and his teacher gave him 18. Sami then donated 236 stamps to the school club, so Lia now has more stamps than Sami. How many stamps does Sami have now?
w10_T4_003163: In the morning a cafe had 82 cupcakes on the counter and sold 58 of them. In the afternoon 14 more were sold, and 4 were dropped and thrown away. In the evening the cupcakes still on the counter were shared equally among the 6 staff, including Mia and Jo. Jo had eaten more cupcakes during the day than Mia. How many cupcakes did Mia get in the evening?
w10_T4_003164: A printer prepared a booklet from 124 large sheets. Each sheet was folded into 2 leaves, and each leaf carries 2 pages of text. He added 26 index pages to the booklet. The printer's shop has 3 presses. He printed 5 copies of the complete booklet, then split all the printed pages into 2 equal boxes and sent one box to the client. How many pages were in the box sent to the client?
w10_T4_003165: Dina's orchard has 71 rows of 9 apple trees, and each tree gave 9 kilograms of apples this year. Her total harvest, once she added in the two orchards she rents, came to triple that amount. She sold 8116 kilograms to a juice factory and 1839 kilograms at the market. Her cousin Eko has fewer kilograms of apples left than Dina. How many kilograms of apples does Dina have left?
w10_T4_003166: In the morning a greengrocer set out 161 boxes of pears with 5 pears in each box, and a farmer brought 70 more pears for the display. In the afternoon 136 pears were sold. In the evening a restaurant bought every pear still on display at 8 cents each and added a 9-cent tip; the greengrocer counts in cents although a hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents did the greengrocer receive from the restaurant?
w10_T4_003168: Kit's marble bag held 35 marbles. He won 20 marbles at recess, found 17 in the sandpit, and was given 44 by his cousin, all going into the bag. The bag is 15 centimetres wide. He then divided the marbles into 2 equal bags and gave one bag to his sister. On the way home he lost 50 marbles through a hole in his bag. How many marbles does Kit have now?
w10_T4_003169: In the morning 41 students were in the drama club room. Before break 10 students left for a music lesson, and 17 left for sports practice. In the afternoon 24 students arrived for rehearsal, and 6 went home early. The room has 8 windows. In the evening every student still in the room was given 3 tickets for the show. How many tickets were given out?
